category_title: Students who disrupt instruction to avoid difficult independent tasks
scenario_title: Transition to independent practice of new math content
minimal_context: Jay is sitting at his desk in his third-grade classroom as the teacher directs the class to begin their independent math practice worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Alright everyone, we've finished going over the new math concepts. It's time to begin your independent practice on the worksheet at your desks.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Fails to attempt his individual seatwork and blurts out loudly) This is too hard! I'm not doing this!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Jay, please focus on your own paper and try to start the first problem.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Bellows across the room) I said I don't know how to do it! It's impossible!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just do your best and keep trying.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Persistently calls out and bellows, causing disruptions to the point where other students complain, while still failing to attempt the seatwork) I need help! You have to show me! I'm not doing it!
